thread:
Anna L.: Hey infra folks — saw a couple failed applies this morning. GH Actions kicked off a terraform job while Atlantis still had a lock; plan worked but apply errored with lock held. Anyone else seeing race between gha and atlantis?

Mike H.: yup saw that on #infra-deploy earlier. Looks like our gha workflow triggers on pushes and also on PR merges; atlantis triggers on PR comments. If a merge happens fast gha can start before the atlantis apply releases the lock.

Ryan C.: can we just rely on Atlantis for applies and make gha only run static checks (fmt/validate/chekcsums)? I like gha for unit tests but we should avoid dual apply paths.

Anna L.: Ideally yes — gha should not run `terraform apply` for infra repos anymore. But some repos still have legacy `apply` jobs. I'm thinking we either 1) enforce `concurrency` in GH Actions to serialize infra runs per repo/ref, or 2) add a cheap preflight that checks Atlantis lock via API and exits if locked. Thoughts?

Mike H.: both are viable. GH Actions `concurrency` is easiest: e.g.
```
concurrency:
  group: infra-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false
```
That prevents two workflows for same ref. But doesn't coordinate with Atlantis if Atlantis uses its own workers.

Ryan C.: preflight against Atlantis API feels more robust: GH runs a tiny script that calls Atlantis `GET /locks` (we host atlantis behind auth) and waits or aborts. We tried this pattern with nomad jobs.

Anna L.: good point. Also, Atlantis has config for `parallel_apply` (terraform.yaml) — turning that off will serialize applies on Atlantis side but won't stop GH starting.

Mike H.: Another option: set GH Action to `needs: atlantis-apply` or use a webhook from Atlantis to kick off GH when apply is done. But that changes flow a lot.

atlantis-bot: INFO: Atlantis lock found for repo=services/payments, user=ryan.c, created=2026-03-17T08:12:03Z

Ryan C.: ^ example — that was my apply earlier. GH started on merge event 5s after I hit apply. Preflight with retry+backoff would have prevented the GH job.

Mike H.: here's a tiny preflight script we can drop into gha:
```
# check-atlantis-lock.sh
for i in {1..6}; do
  resp=$(curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $ATLANTIS_TOKEN" "https://atlantis.company.internal/api/v1/locks?repo=${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}") || true
  if echo "$resp" | grep -q "no locks"; then
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "atlantis locked, retrying... ($i)"
  sleep $((i * 5))
done
exit 2
```
Works fine and exits non-zero if locked after retries.

Anna L.: Nice. Couple extra asks: 1) GH runners need network access to atlantis internal endpoint — some self-hosted runners do, others not. 2) we should surface nicer failures in pipeline logs so devs don't get confused.

Ryan C.: For self-hosted runner gaps we can fallback to the concurrency approach. Add both: preflight when atlantis reachable else rely on `concurrency`.

Mike H.: Also, ArgoCD sync can conflict if we rely on Helm chart updates that include generated tfstate values. Recommend we add an ArgoCD webhook subscription to Atlantis so once Atlantis finishes apply it triggers a sync on the corresponding k8s-app. That reduces drift.

Anna L.: Agreed. For ArgoCD, we can use the argocd-app-of-apps pattern and set `syncPolicy.automated.prune=false` initially. Or use resource hooks to wait for CRDs to be ready. But first step is to stop GH duplicate applies.

Ryan C.: I'll open a PR that: 1) removes `apply` jobs from gha infra workflows where possible, 2) adds the preflight script + `concurrency` as fallback, 3) updates README w/ flow diagram.

Mike H.: I'll draft the Atlantis config change (disable parallel_apply for services/*) and add logging for lock owner in webhook payload.

Anna L.: sweet. @deploy-bot can you add an entry in deploy-runbook for "gha vs atlantis apply" and a troubleshooting checklist (check atlantis locks, check runner network)? :slightly_smiling_face:

deploy-bot: ✅ Added checklist to /runbooks/infra/gha-atlantis.md — PR 245 created (will auto-merge in 24h).

Anna L.: Thanks all — let's track in the PRs. If anyone sees a regression ping here. :thumbsup:
